integrity: The non-Gibbs conclusion is obtained analytically from the exact regular-tree hard-core recursion together with the primary source two-layer transfer.
Finite numerical cavity iterations are corroborative only and are not used to infer the infinite-volume phase transition.
The statement distinguishes the exact onset of the all-zero witness from the unknown full Gibbs/non-Gibbs boundary.
scientific_limitations: The theorem proves non-quasilocality for \(p>p_{\mathrm{hc}}(d)\) but does not prove Gibbsianness for all \(p\le p_{\mathrm{hc}}(d)\).
It concerns regular Cayley trees of order at least two and the all-zero second-layer witness.
A weakly indexed equivalent corollary of the hard-core uniqueness theorem remains a residual originality risk.
title: Exact onset of the hidden hard-core discontinuity under isolate removal on regular trees
